page: Amazon Web Services m8g.16xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro System and powered by 64-bit ARMv9 architecture. The instance provides 64 dedicated physical cores based on the AWS Neoverse-V2 design operating at 2.8 GHz, running one thread per core without hyperthreading contention. Backed by 256 GB of system memory, the platform maintains a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. The instance includes 30 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth and operates without local storage, relying entirely on network-attached Amazon EBS volumes.

Benchmark results highlight strong multi-threaded scaling and memory throughput across data-intensive tasks. The system achieves top-tier results in uncached read memory bandwidth at 464.59 GB/sec, uncached write bandwidth at 224.93 GB/sec, and Clang compilation benchmarks. Multi-threaded decompression and Redis throughput also reach top-tier percentiles, processing 131.7 million operations per second. However, single-core execution metrics across stress-ng and Geekbench fall within the average range, indicating that raw single-thread speed is secondary to aggregate parallel capacity.

The 64-core single-thread architecture provides consistent execution by eliminating noisy-neighbor resource competition between sibling threads. In exchange, the platform requires all persistent and high-speed temporary storage to transit network links due to the absence of bundled NVMe drives, which can introduce latency boundaries in extreme I/O pipelines. The balance of network bandwidth, dense core counts, and high memory bandwidth fits enterprise microservices, clustered databases, large-scale software compilation, in-memory caching, and static web serving fleets.
description: Amazon Web Services m8g.16xlarge is an arm64 general-purpose instance powered by AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 processors running at 2.8 GHz. Delivering 64 dedicated physical cores without simultaneous multithreading, it features 256 GB of memory, a balanced 4.0 GB per vCPU ratio, and 30 Gbps baseline network throughput. The instance includes no local storage, requiring external Amazon EBS volumes for file systems. Benchmark evaluations demonstrate top-tier uncached memory bandwidth exceeding 464 GB/sec for reads, rapid software compilation under Clang, and exceptional multi-threaded throughput in Redis SET operations and static web serving. While single-thread benchmark results remain mid-tier, the 64-core dedicated topology excels in parallel execution consistency. The m8g.16xlarge is suited for high-concurrency enterprise workloads including distributed databases, CI/CD compilation pipelines, container orchestration clusters, and high-throughput web backends.
